claims.says: README: 'Research prototype for reference only, not an official DeepSeek product.' 'Treat it as research code, not production-ready software.' Repo sidebar: MIT license. Published by the deepseek-ai GitHub organisation. Said as: DeepSeek has shared a research prototype, open on GitHub, under the MIT license; a research prototype, not an official DeepSeek product, and not ready for production.

README: 'a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository' ... 'It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu.' Deployment doc: a new mention arrives on the next poll, one minute by default. Said as: it keeps listening to one GitHub repository, and if you want, to a team chat app (Feishu, not named).

Deployment doc: open an Issue or post a comment containing '@<agent login> <request>' from an allowed account; 'until a list has someone, no request can become a Ticket'. Said as: someone on an allowed list writes a comment with the agent's name and a request; until that list has someone in it, no request is accepted.

Execution doc: 'Each Ticket gets an Executor Session named worker-<ticket id> and a directory named after the Ticket's short name.' Said as: each accepted request becomes a ticket; every ticket gets its own worker session, in its own folder.

README: it 'answers in the original conversation, for example with a pull request. A web panel shows what needs a person.' Execution doc: 'By default, the Executor never enables auto-merge as the agent account.' Said as: it answers in the same conversation, for example with a pull request; it does not turn on auto-merge by default; a web panel shows what needs a person.

README: 'Some designs discussed in the article are directions for future development and are not implemented in this prototype.' (the article: Exploring Super-agent Design). Said as: some ideas from their article are not built yet.

Execution doc: 'Executor Sessions run commands without approval as the operator's OS user.' Deployment doc: 'Both presets run with danger-full-access as the operator's OS user.' Said as: the workers run commands without asking, as the computer user who runs the agent.

Deployment doc: 'A worker can execute programs by path and read the operator's home directory. For isolation, use a dedicated OS account containing only the agent's credentials.' Said as: a worker can read that user's home folder; the guide says give the agent its own account, with only its own keys.

Framing, not a fact: 'not a developer that works alone; a map of how agents could keep working between your prompts' follows the README's own status (research prototype, reference only) and its rule that it acts only when asked or when a team rule allows it.
